task.title: Host check does not pin a host on non-loopback board binds, and the README says it does
task.description:
Follow-up from the adversarial review of PR #27 (WB-01KZBT0R3KS9DCFGSRP2J7C22X, merged as 43d7cbb). Deferred as minor because PR #27's acceptance criterion is scoped to loopback ("not the bound loopback host and port"), which the merged code meets, and the code comment at internal/webui/guard.go:78-83 is honest about the tradeoff. The defect is that the README documents a stronger guarantee than the code delivers.

What the code does. In originGuard.reject (internal/webui/guard.go:100-115) the Host test is:

    if !ok || port != guard.port || (guard.loopback && !loopbackHost(host))

When guard.loopback is false the host is never compared to anything, only the port is. originIsBoard (internal/webui/guard.go:120-135) then falls back to strings.EqualFold(trimRootDot(host), trimRootDot(requestHost)) -- the Origin is checked against the *request's own* Host -- so a rebound name satisfies both checks by matching itself.

Verified empirically against main at 3bbe22b. Built GuardSameOrigin(inner, bound) for bound in {0.0.0.0:7331, [::]:7331, 192.168.1.5:7331} and sent GET /api/tasks with Host: evil.example:7331, then POST /api/tasks with Host: evil.example:7331, Origin: http://evil.example:7331, Content-Type: application/json. All six requests returned 200 and reached the inner handler. Control: the same GET against a 127.0.0.1:7331 bind returns 403 and does not reach the inner handler, so loopback binds are correctly protected.

Impact. A teammate runs 'workbook serve --addr 0.0.0.0:7331'. Any page on the internet rebinds its own DNS name to the victim's LAN address and gains same-origin read *and write* on the board. Writes publish through boardPublisher to origin, reach every teammate's clone, and are later read by coding agents as work instructions -- the prompt-injection channel WB-01KZBT0R3KS9DCFGSRP2J7C22X was filed to close, reachable from off-network rather than only from the LAN. The existing exposure warning (boardExposureWarning, exercised at internal/cli/run_test.go:1754) says the board has 'no authentication', which concedes LAN reachability but not that an arbitrary remote page can drive it.

Suggested resolution, either:
1. Correct README.md (the guard section around lines 740-760). It currently states flatly 'The Host header must name the address the listener bound' and 'every route is subject to all three', which a reader will take as covering non-loopback binds. Say instead that off loopback the Host check pins only the port, and strengthen the exposure warning to name remote drive-by access rather than just missing authentication.
2. Additionally, for an explicit-IP bind such as --addr 192.168.1.5:7331 the reachable address *is* known, so the Host can be pinned to that literal. Only a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0 / [::]) genuinely cannot know which names reach it. That would shrink the gap to wildcard binds alone.

Regression tests should cover a foreign Host against an explicit-IP bind and against a wildcard bind, so the documented behavior and the actual behavior stay in agreement.
